newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 18.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Norwiegan King Harald V and Queen Sonja will arrive in Prague today. The king will meet with members of the Czech cabinet.

- Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus visited Budapest, Hungary yesterday accompanied by Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka to meet with the Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and other senior officials.
- An agreement was closed between the Agriculture and Finance Ministries in the past few days for the transfer of shares of Restitucni Investicni Fond for 800 million crowns.
- The compulsory administrator of Agrobanka, Jiri Klumpar, reacted to speculation from Motoinvest that during compulsory administration, the state added to the bank's losses.
- The new owner of Cechofracht will be announced on April 4. According to the general director, Stanislav Mach, the tender for Cechofracht was closed yesterday.
LIDOVE NOVINY - President Vaclav Havel returned a proposed water law back to parliament yesterday. The law was approved by parliament on February 28.

- Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka will present a proposal to the cabinet today for raising pensions on average by 8.1 percent and social support on average by 5.5 percent, effective from July 1.

- Energeticke Centrum Kladno (ECK) plans to go through with its proposal to announce bankruptcy on Poldi Steel. Poldi owes ECK more than 300 million crowns, but its majority owner, Pro Win, has not yet met with ECK about settling the debt.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Health Minister Jan Strasky presented a new proposal for health reforms to the cabinet yesterday. If it is approved, patients are in store for additional charges.
- The Defence Ministry has chosen Unysis as the supplier for a military staff information system, a decision which has taken two years, two tenders and various problems, army sources say.
- Belgian Kredietbank increased its stake in Banka Hana to 18.8 percent from nearly nine percent originally.
- The C.S. Fond investigation will be joined by the counter espionage services.

PRAVO - Three foreign investors from Germany and the United States show interest in a property share of Poldi. The first is Annahutte-Max Aicher from Germany. The other two are Metcon-Mukerjee and Coudert Brothers with Maluga Stahl.
- During this February and March, Karosa Vysoke Myto supplied five articulated buses and 39 normal buses to Lithuania, a deal worth nearly four million dollars.
